prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one level of a derelict ghost ship (a dungeon) in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE LOWER DECK OF A DERELICT GHOST SHIP, seen from above: a long central corridor of old wooden planks from a ladder in the west to steps down in the east; on both sides small crew cabins divided by wooden bulkheads, each with a door opening onto the corridor: torn hammocks, sea chests, a table with a lantern, broken bunks, a galley with water barrels; a corner flooded with sea water; the curved hull timbers around. Palette: dark browns, grey-green damp wood, dim teal water. Cramped, eerie, abandoned.

IMPORTANT SHIP SHAPE: this is the inside of a real sailing ship seen from above: the bow end (east) narrows to ONE smooth, gracefully curved point, the hull walls follow smooth continuous curves; NEVER a stepped, staircase or blocky outline anywhere, no right-angle notches in the hull walls. The guide's stepped bow is only a rough placement: smooth it within the tolerance. The straight inner bulkheads and cabin walls stay straight.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 48 x 28 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2304 x 1344 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no houses, piers, ships or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, meadows, rocks and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- brown with plank lines = the walkable wooden DECK / floor of the ship: old dark planks, grey-green with age and damp, a few loose boards, rope coils flat on the deck.
- dark reddish with block lines = an old faded CARPET / rug on the floor (walkable).
- grey with arcs = puddles of bilge and wet planks (walkable).
- teal = sea water that has flooded in through the broken hull (not walkable).
- dark brown with lines = the ship's WALLS, bulkheads, the hull sides and the RAILS (not walkable): thick timbers and ribs.
- the darkest brown-black = the space outside / under the ship (not walkable): shadowed hull timbers.
- deep dark blue = the sea around the ship (not walkable): dark swell, drifts of pale fog on the water.
- grey circles = crates, barrels, fallen rigging (not walkable).
The walls and bulkheads follow the guide exactly; the ship's rooms are straight-sided (it is a built ship), but the hull outline is a smooth curved ship shape.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(40,26,16) = a LADDER going up through a square hole in the ceiling.
- the blocks in colour rgb(40,26,16) = narrow wooden STEPS going down into the dark hold.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, boats or ships on the water (unless a landmark says so), treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt: Generate ONE complete finished 2304×1344 top-down fantasy JRPG dungeon game-map image, using the FIRST user-attached image as a STRICT spatial tracing/layout guide (not as style), and SECOND user-attached image ONLY as the pixel-art style reference. Preserve the guide's overall ship position, scale, corridor width and all narrow door gaps, bulkheads, rooms, flooding and two black stair/ladder positions precisely. This is the lower deck interior of one derelict sailing ship, overhead orthographic RPG view (south-facing thickness visible on timber walls), NOT isometric/perspective. Render premium richly detailed sharp hand-placed square-pixel art with distinct crisp pixel clusters, warm dark outlines, hue-shifted ramps, same detail scale as style reference; no soft blending, antialiasing, blur or noise. The west-to-east central wooden-plank corridor runs through the center, with square upward ladder opening at the WEST end and narrow descending timber stair opening at the EAST end. Along BOTH sides, exactly FIVE rectangular rooms separated by straight narrow timber bulkheads with door-sized openings onto corridor at positions shown in guide; respect all precisely. Ancient gray-green weathered planks and dark damp brown floorboards, weather stains, sparse flat ropes, occasional loose boards, water marks and discreet small debris only where it doesn't impede walking. In the southeastern room paint the irregular nonwalkable teal seawater flooded patch at the exact position and extent of the guide. Thick curved hull walls/ribs hug the outside perimeter; unlike the guide's rough staircase silhouette, EAST/BOW hull narrows in ONE smooth graceful continuous curved taper ending in ONE point, NO blocky stair steps or right-angle notches in outer ship silhouette; retain straight-sided internal built room walls. A little suggested torn hammocks and broken bunks fixed against cabin edges and water barrels in the galley in available nonwalking pockets only; leave corridor and all doorways unobstructed. Surrounding exterior in deep brown-black shadowed hull timber with subtle sea-blue at outermost water if appropriate, no hard frame. Ship is eerie and abandoned but ALBEDO neutral even daylight appearance; balanced legible palette of damp gray-green timber, dark rich brown ribs, dim teal water. No characters, boats or ships on water, treasure chests, lanterns, torches, fire, lettering, labels, grid, border, vignette, light pools, glow, or fog overlay. Particularly important: reproduce FIRST IMAGE's exact floorplan, not a new imagined floor plan.
